2_rows_per_second_null_by_layer.population: every asset_throughput row, grouped by 2-char asset_id prefix (bg/ga/bo/ka/ph/mi)
2_rows_per_second_null_by_layer.query: SELECT substring(asset_id from 1 for 2) AS prefix, count(*) total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE rows_per_second IS NULL) null_rps, round(100.0*count(*) FILTER (WHERE rows_per_second IS NULL)/count(*),1) pct_null FROM asset_throughput GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
2_rows_per_second_null_by_layer.correction_to_stated_assumption: The campaign brief's framing ('rows_per_second is reportedly NULL for every one of the 40 L0 assets') UNDERSTATES the finding. rows_per_second is NULL for 100% of ALL 268 rows across ALL SIX layers, not just L0's 39. Confirmed independently by re-running the same NULL check restricted to rows whose most recent build_run_assets disposition was a genuine 'build' (not a skip): 64/64 still NULL (see figure 5 below). No writer in any layer, and no code path anywhere in the engine, has ever computed this column (see code-write-sites — the only reference to rows_per_second in the entire codebase outside migrations/tests is a read in a governance census script that reports it as a missing signal). This is an engine-wide gap, not an L0-specific one. Separately: L0 (bg) itself has only 39 asset_throughput rows although asset_registry lists 40 bg assets — bg_gochara_citation_resolution has NO throughput row at all (never built/tracked), so 'NULL for every one of the 40' is imprecise in the other direction too: 39 are NULL, 1 doesn't exist as a row to be NULL.

3_duration_column_null_by_layer.value: NOT APPLICABLE on asset_throughput — no duration column exists there to be NULL (see schema section). On build_run_assets, the closest existing pair (started_at, ended_at) is fully populated for state='complete' (3159/3159 = 100%), largely populated for state='error' on ended_at (1564/1565 = 99.9%) but sparse for error's started_at (324/1565 = 20.7%), and sparse for state='aborted' on both (started_at 8/706 = 1.1%, ended_at 406/706 = 57.5%, both-present 7/706 = 1.0%).
3_duration_column_null_by_layer.query: SELECT state, count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE started_at IS NOT NULL) has_started, count(*) FILTER (WHERE ended_at IS NOT NULL) has_ended, count(*) FILTER (WHERE started_at IS NOT NULL AND ended_at IS NOT NULL) has_both FROM build_run_assets GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
3_duration_column_null_by_layer.interpretation: Duration is ALREADY fully derivable today for every completed build (ended_at - started_at, 100% coverage, sample durations range 0.038s to 212.2s in the last 8 completions checked). This materially changes A1's implementation: for the 'complete' case there is no new timing capture needed at all, only a rate computation + a write into asset_throughput.rows_per_second. Duration IS a genuine gap for 'aborted' (99% missing started_at) and partially for 'error' (79% missing started_at) — those are the honest attribution gaps A1 should name, not silently paper over with a derived duration that doesn't exist.

code_write_sites.note: Every distinct engine code path (Python orchestrator, legacy L1 writer telemetry, and Next.js cockpit routes) that INSERTs or UPDATEs asset_throughput or touches build_substep_progress, found by grepping for literal 'INSERT INTO'/'UPDATE' against these table names across platform/python-sidecar and platform/src, excluding test files and one-off dispatch/migration scripts.

orchestrator_core_python.does: INSERT ... state='error', message='BLOCKED: upstream...' (chart-scoped branch). Cascade-failure marking, no timing/rate touched.
INSERT ... state='error' (global-asset else branch). Same as above.
UPDATE ... state='error' for every row still 'building' when a fresh run acquires the chart lock (orphan-from-crash reap). No rate touched; rows_written untouched (retains whatever it was).
UPDATE ... state='stale' for downstream assets, self-joined against pre-UPDATE snapshot to log prev_state. No rows_written/rate touched.
INSERT recovery row (chart-scoped) when a state UPDATE matched 0 rows. Sets state/last_error/last_built_at only.
INSERT recovery row (global else branch), same shape.

UPDATE state='error', last_error=%s, last_built_at=NOW(). THE failure-path write. rows_written is deliberately NOT touched here — it retains its previous value. This is the honest-null anchor point: no rate is ever computed on this path, by construction, today.
UPDATE state='lit', last_built_at=NOW(), rows_written=0 (GREEN branch — service assets deliberately record 0 rows by design, this is NOT a defect for storage_type='service').

UPDATE last_built_at=NOW(), rows_written=<cumulative> after EACH substep (heartbeat, keeps the watchdog from reaping a long-running heavy writer). THIS is the natural home for per-substep duration/rate if A1 adds it — it already has cumulative rows_written and a timestamp per iteration, so a rows-since-last-heartbeat / seconds-since-last-heartbeat rate is directly computable here without a new column, by diffing against the row's own previous last_built_at before overwriting it.
UPDATE state='lit', rows_written=COALESCE(rows_written,0) (skip-if-green: writer not run at all, so 0/unchanged rows is correct).
UPDATE state='lit', last_built_at=NOW(), last_error=NULL. rows_written NOT touched (correctly retains prior value on a legitimate skip).

THE MAIN COMPLETION WRITE: UPDATE state=%s, last_built_at=NOW(), rows_written=%s, built_against_upstream_hash=%s, built_against_writer_hash=%s, last_error=NULL. This is where A1's new duration+rate columns need to be set for the success path — rows_written is already computed as (rows_inserted+rows_updated) at this point (line ~1073), and a duration is available by reading back this row's own pre-overwrite last_built_at (set at the 'building' transition, see next entry) OR — more robustly, since last_built_at gets clobbered on every heartbeat during _drive_substeps — by reading build_run_assets.started_at for this (run_id, asset_id), which is untouched by heartbeats.

INSERT/UPSERT state='building', last_built_at=NOW() at the START of the asset's execution (chart-scoped branch). Comment in-source ('WATCHDOG HEARTBEAT FIX') confirms this is the canonical build-start timestamp — but it lands in the SAME column (last_built_at) that the completion UPDATE (line 1195) later overwrites, so asset_throughput alone cannot yield duration; the start timestamp is lost by the time of completion unless captured into a local variable or read from build_run_assets.started_at (which IS preserved, see schema finding 3).
Same INSERT/UPSERT, global-asset (chart_id IS NULL) else branch.

legacy_L1_writer_telemetry_python.does: INSERT/UPSERT state, rows_written, last_measured_build_id, last_built_at=NOW(), last_measured_at=NOW(). Explicitly documented in its own docstring as a SEPARATE, best-effort, exception-swallowing path used by several ga_writers/*.py files (ga_strength_writer.py, ga_vargas_writer.py, ga_sade_sati_writer.py, ga_panchanga_writer.py, ga_sensitive_writer.py, ga_positions_writer.py, ga_dashas_writer.py) — this bypasses the orchestrator's own asset_runner.py completion write entirely for L1 (ga_*) writers. It sets last_measured_at (suggesting a 'measurement' concept already exists in naming) but NEVER computes or sets rows_per_second — confirming the gap is not a bug in an existing rate computation, it is that no rate computation exists anywhere, in either the orchestrator path or this legacy L1 path.
legacy_L1_writer_telemetry_python.risk_for_A1: A1 must patch BOTH this shared helper AND asset_runner.py's write sites, or L1 (ga_*) assets will keep reporting NULL rate/duration after L2-L5 assets start reporting real values — an inconsistency the packet should watch for.

cockpit_typescript_routes.does: INSERT ... state='dormant' placeholder row, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET updated_at=now() — wrapped in .catch(()=>null) with an explicit source comment 'non-fatal: table may not have updated_at column'. CONFIRMED: asset_throughput has NO updated_at column, so this ON CONFLICT clause silently no-ops on every conflict today — an existing, already-acknowledged dead branch, unrelated to A1 but worth flagging as a nearby honest-signal smell (§N.8-adjacent): the .catch() makes a real failure indistinguishable from success.
UPDATE state='dormant', last_built_at=NULL, rows_written=0 (reset after a clear operation, chart-scoped).
UPDATE state='stale' for downstream assets after a clear.
UPDATE state='lit', rows_written=$3, last_error=NULL, last_built_at=NOW() — reaper recovering a heartbeat-alive-but-orphaned build using its last known substep rows count. No rate touched.
UPDATE state='incomplete', rows_written=$3, last_built_at=NOW(), last_error=... — reaper marking a stale-heartbeat build incomplete.

UPDATE state='dormant', last_built_at=NULL, rows_written=NULL (pre-rebuild clear, chart-scoped).

build_substep_progress_writers.note: Only 3 writer-owned files touch this table directly — the generic orchestrator substep driver (_drive_substeps in asset_runner.py) does NOT read or write it, and its own `completed_keys` resume parameter is never populated from this table in the current production call path (grep-confirmed: `_drive_substeps(...)` is invoked once, at asset_runner.py:1043, without a completed_keys argument, so it always defaults to an empty set today — the 'resume, skip already-finished substeps' capability described in the driver's own docstring is currently dead for every writer except the 3 below, which implement their own private resumability using this table.

sites.does: INSERT (chart_id, asset_id, substep_key, build_fingerprint, rows_written, completed_at=now()) ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE. Reads back via _load_completed_substeps (own method, line ~2448). Only completed_at is stored — no started_at, so no per-substep duration exists here either despite this table being the closest thing to a 'substep timing' surface in the schema.

rows_per_second.finding: No code path anywhere in the engine computes rows_per_second. It is not a broken detector producing a wrong value — it is the complete absence of a detector. Confirmed by exhaustive grep: the only non-migration, non-test reference to the string 'rows_per_second' in the whole repository is in platform/scripts/governance/asset_census.py, which READS it (as a health-signal check flagging it missing) but never writes it.
rows_per_second.what_A1_must_ensure: If A1 adds a rate computation, it must be placed ONLY on success-completing write sites (asset_runner.py:1195 _run_data_writer, :636 service GREEN probe [rate is meaningless for 0-row service asset, should stay NULL], :849 _mark_probe_green [skip-no-rows, should stay NULL], and the legacy ga_writers/_telemetry.py path) and explicitly NEVER on mark_asset_error (line 584), the orphan-crash reap (runner.py:1127), or the watchdog's truly-stuck error path (watchdog/route.ts:330) — those three are the paths that must produce a real, correctly-false 'no rate recorded' (NULL), because a failed or aborted build has no valid duration to divide rows by. This is directly checkable: today none of those three failure paths touch rows_written or any new rate column, which is the right shape to preserve.

duration.detector_exists_today: PARTIALLY — via build_run_assets.started_at/ended_at for the 'complete' state (100% populated), but genuinely does not exist for 'aborted' (started_at 1.1% populated) and is weak for 'error' (started_at 20.7% populated).
duration.what_A1_must_ensure: A duration figure for an aborted/most error builds must render as NULL/'not recorded', not 0 or a wrong-but-plausible number, because 79-99% of those rows are missing the timestamp needed to compute it honestly. If A1's implementation back-fills a duration for these rows by any proxy (e.g. defaulting started_at to created_at or ended_at when missing), that would be exactly the '5.0-on-computed-zero-grade' class of invented-judgment defect §N.7 item 6 warns against.

contradictions_of_stated_campaign_assump: The brief's framing that rows_per_second is NULL 'for every one of the 40 L0 assets' is too narrow: it is NULL for ALL 268 asset_throughput rows across ALL SIX layers (100%, not just L0), with zero exceptions found by any disposition or state cut. This is an engine-wide gap, not an L0-specific one, and both A1's scope and its acceptance criteria should say so.

L0 (bg) has only 39 asset_throughput rows, not 40 — bg_gochara_citation_resolution (present in asset_registry) has never been tracked at all (no row, not even a NULL one). This asset would need special handling in any before/after diff keyed on 'the 40 L0 assets'.

The 'rows_written reads 0 for ~10 of them [L0 assets]' claim is CONFIRMED, and more precisely bounded than stated: 9 of L0's 12 zero/null rows are verified-populated-target-but-recorded-zero (a defect); a 10th matching case (ka_gochara_v3_century_materialize) exists but is in L3 (ka_), not L0; one L0 case (bg_sarvatobhadra_grid) is genuinely, honestly empty and must not be 'fixed' to a nonzero value.

The brief's premise that build_substep_progress 'already has the hook' for substep-level timing does not hold: the table has no started_at/duration column (only completed_at), and the generic orchestrator substep driver does not use this table at all today (only 3 specific L3 writers write to it privately, for their own resumability, also without timing). Any substep-level timing feature is new work, not wiring an existing hook.

A genuinely-usable duration hook DOES already exist, just not where the brief pointed: build_run_assets.started_at/ended_at, 100% populated for completed builds. This is very likely cheaper for A1 to build on than adding new columns to asset_throughput or build_substep_progress.

rows_per_second is not read or displayed anywhere in the served application (zero hits in platform/src for 'rows_per_second'/'rowsPerSecond' outside tests) — populating it will not visibly change any UI surface unless a consuming display is also added; this may or may not be in A1's scope and is worth confirming before claiming the packet 'done'.

A separate, active write path exists for L1 (ga_*) writers — platform/python-sidecar/ga_writers/_telemetry.py — that bypasses the orchestrator's own asset_runner.py completion write. A1 must patch both paths or L1 assets will lag L2-L5 in reporting real rate/duration after this packet ships.
